To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

PCB patterns are determined by equilibrium distribution between tissues and the environment, that PCBs are mobilized from organs whose lipid content increases and that the plateau-values of PCB concentrations in the various organs decline in time.

the relative contributions of PCB components to total PCB in organs were virtually identical in a 275 day period, and that concentrations of PCBs in organs on lipid basis decreased in a 275day period.
PCB components in organs of sole are determined by equilibrium-partitioning and that the plateau-values of PCB concentrations on lipid basis decrease in all organs.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the kinetics of PCBs in fish.
the question of how PCBs are distributed in fish.
PCBs in sole and their relation to lipid metabolism.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
individual PCB components in organs were mobilized from lipid stores and partitioned to other lipid stores, but that the partitioning coefficients were different for individual components and organs.
PCB components were mobilized from organs whose lipid content increased, and from organs whose lipid composition changed.
PCB components in organs were determined by a combination of equilibrium partitioning and mobilization from organs whose lipid content increased.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the kinetics of individual PCB components is determined by their partitioning behaviour in relation to the lipid content of organs.

in juvenile soles PCB components are taken up from food, distributed in all organs and stored in lipophilic tissues in relation to the equilibrium partitioning of the various components between lipids and lipids in tissues.
PCB components in soles are mobilizable and can be transferred to organs with increasing lipid contents, but are not necessarily taken up by organs whose lipid contents increase.
The main takeaway from our work is that
individual PCB components in fish can be mobilised from the various organs.
the kinetics of PCB components is not related to the lipid metabolism of the organism.
PCBs are stored in the various organs in a pattern determined by their partitioning into lipids.
